papers.title: Intrinsic Geometry Matching: learning observation-equivariant process geometry
papers.abstract: Real data are often arbitrary, indirect observations of an unknown underlying process, and those observations can distort its geometry. Existing geometric methods equip data with the induced geometry of the ambient space, but this entangles the true geometry of the process with the distortion of the observation. To address this, we introduce Intrinsic Geometry Matching (IGM): a scalable approach to learn the intrinsic geometry of the underlying process. Specifically, we learn the carr\'e du champ operator of the process, allowing us to recover its diffusion geometry. Our method uses the fact that data often come with natural perturbations, like steps in a time series, to recover the intrinsic carr\'e du champ while transforming naturally with changes in observation: it is observation-equivariant. Furthermore, since this equivariance relates the geometry of different spaces, we can train a model using additional sources of data, even when that data lies in another space. We evaluate IGM on molecular dynamics, image, and video data and find better performance and scaling than existing neural and graph-based geometric tools.

papers.title: Beyond Cultural Persona Bias: Response Geometry as a Measure for Language Models and People
papers.abstract: Researchers are increasingly prompting language models with cultural personas so that they answer questionnaires as diverse human groups would. However, studies often report that these persona responses do not predict the models' behavior. We argue that whether the persona is Western or non-Western, the model's answers carry a cultural preference, and that this preference masks the variables that could predict its behavior. We examine the prompted preference at two levels: aggregate Big Five scores and response geometry, the correlation matrix between dimensions within each respondent, represented as a symmetric positive-definite (SPD) matrix. In DeepSeek-V3 and GPT-4o, when the item order is fixed, the prompted preference appears at both levels. Randomizing item order reduces it in the response geometry, while leaving it in the Big Five scores: the Big Five still separate the two personas at $95$--$97\%$, while response geometry falls to chance. In randomized administration, the response geometry still contains information about the respondent. In DeepSeek-V4-Flash, SPD features are associated with whether the same instance sorts Asian American public figures as ``foreign'' in a text IAT ($p = .047$), while the Big Five do not. In human studies conducted using randomized item order, the response geometry identifies people from test-retest sessions in $81$ -- $85\%$, against chance $0.4\%$, and predicts sex and, weakly, age. In addition, SPD features also predict complex human behavior (e.g., cumulative GPA, $R^2 = 0.28$, permutation $p = .003$), where the Big Five do not.

papers.title: A Half-Space Theorem for the Allen--Cahn Equation in All Dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove that, in every dimension, a bounded, non-constant entire solution of the Allen--Cahn equation whose zero set is contained in a half-space is a one-dimensional heteroclinic solution.

papers.title: Spectral G\aa rding Elliptic Equations
papers.abstract: We study spectral G\aa rding elliptic equations on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Smooth solvability is equivalent to the existence of a smooth representative in the admissible domain. The concavity theorem for ideal G\aa rding polynomials gives a fixed concave formulation to which Sz\'ekelyhidi's second-order argument applies in every degree $2\le d\le n$, extending Lin's top-degree solvability theorem. Combined with the numerical criteria of Fu--Li--Zhang--Zhang and Chen--Nie--Xu, this yields a Nakai--Moishezon type criterion for solvability on compact K\"ahler manifolds. A solution converts the local ideal G\aa rding structure into a global Lorentzian structure. Its mixed derivatives give a strict nonlinear Hodge--Riemann hierarchy from the degree of the equation down to degree two, and the homogenization of the intersection polynomial is Lorentzian in nef class directions. Numerical criteria then produce explicit Hodge--Riemann classes, Lefschetz isomorphisms in bidegree $(1,1)$, and weighted Hodge-index inequalities.

papers.title: The Brakke-BV structure of flat flows
papers.abstract: We show that, in ambient dimension at most seven, varifold limits of the minimizing movements scheme introduced by Almgren--Taylor--Wang and Luckhaus--Sturzenhecker are integral Brakke flows. As a consequence, we show that $L^1$-limit points of the scheme, usually known as flat flows, are generalized BV flows. The result is unconditional and, in particular, remains valid even in the absence of energy convergence and in the presence of fattening.

papers.title: Sharp stability for mixed bubbles on hyperbolic space
papers.abstract: We prove sharp residual stability estimates for the critical Poincar\'e-Sobolev equation near sums of one positive hyperbolic solution and one projected Euclidean bubble in dimensions at least four. The estimates are uniform in the relative positions of the centers. The sharp rate is linear except in dimension six, where it contains a square root of a logarithm. For nonnegative functions, the same estimates hold under an energy constraint near the sum of the two profile energies for \(\lambda\) outside a finite set, and an additional mass constraint removes this restriction. For arbitrary finite numbers of profiles, we identify and realize all nonnegative Palais-Smale levels. We characterize the parameters at which different pairs of profile numbers have the same energy and show that the limiting energy and mass determine both profile numbers.

papers.title: Regularity theorems for Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the minimal surface system
papers.abstract: We prove several regularity theorems concerning Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the minimal surface system. The main lemma (i.e. ``Decoupling Lemma") says that the component functions of such solutions satisfy the homogeneous Pucci inequalities. This allows us to apply the regularity theory for scalar viscosity solutions for elliptic PDE component-wise to a viscosity solution for the system. As a result of the Decoupling Lemma, we deduce that 2D Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the system are analytic in the interior, and obtain a quantitative partial regularity theorem. We also prove a geometric Harnack inequality for Lipschitz solutions. The Harnack inequality yields a strong maximum principle and half-space Liouville theorem. Another significant consequence of the lemma is a boundary regularity theorem for Lipschitz viscosity solutions. Notably, our theorem does not require any density assumption at the graph boundary, and we do not assume stationarity. This is used to prove a classification theorem for the singular set of a 4D stationary solution on a bounded domain. We also prove an $\varepsilon$-regularity theorem extending a result of the author. To conclude, we survey open problems. As an example, we have included a Bernstein-type theorem for 3D homogeneous entire Lipschitz viscosity solutions. Taken together, our results suggest that viscosity methods are a useful tool for studying the regularity of minimal graphs.

papers.title: Cubic moments of eigenfunctions on surfaces
papers.abstract: We identify Gaussian curvature as a local mechanism for cubic cancellation of Laplace eigenfunctions on Riemannian surfaces, without arithmetic or dynamical assumptions. For $L^2$-normalized local solutions at frequency $\lambda$, cubic integrals against smooth compactly supported weights tend to zero whenever the curvature is nonzero almost everywhere where the weight is nonzero. Finite-order nondegeneracy yields sharp polynomial decay rates. In particular, on closed surfaces with nowhere-vanishing curvature, we obtain the rate $O(\lambda^{-1/6})$, attained by spherical harmonics on the round sphere. This proves the cubic case of the Gaussian moment conjecture for all normalized real eigenfunctions on closed negatively curved surfaces. The local proof rests on an exact identity relating the reduced phase at a Fermat point to Gaussian curvature. On complete hyperbolic surfaces with positive systole, we also prove global $O((\log\lambda)^{-3/2})$ decay for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions and smooth weights with bounded covariant derivatives through order two, without assuming finite area.

papers.title: Minimal time for heat observability on almost-Riemannian surfaces
papers.abstract: We determine the minimal observation time for the heat equation on a closed almost-Riemannian surface, for a class of observation sets leaving sufficiently thin collars around simple Baouendi-Grushin circles. The structure and density are analytic near these circles, and the coefficients may depend on both variables. The formula is expressed through a complex phase describing concentration near the singular set and extends the thresholds known for separated models. Regular unobserved regions away from the circles do not change this time, provided all other singularities are observed. For singular circles of constant bracket step greater than two, local analyticity implies failure of observability at every time for observation sets at positive distance. We also construct quasimodes concentrated near simple singular circles, with exponentially small errors. Their superpositions give a lower bound for the Schr\"odinger observation time.

papers.title: Regularity theory for lattice based harmonic maps and low temperature Gibbs measures of the spin-$O(N)$ model
papers.abstract: The purpose of this note is twofold. First, we revisit the classical regularity theory of harmonic maps in the setting of maps defined on a lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ instead of $\mathbb{R}^d$ or some other manifold. The target space of our harmonic maps will be spheres $\mathbb{S}^{N-1}, N\geq 2$. A harmonic map $\sigma : \mathbb{Z}^d \to \mathbb{S}^{N-1}$ is a map which in any finite subgraph $\Lambda$ minimizes the internal Dirichlet energy $\frac 1 2 \sum_{i \sim j \in \Lambda} \|\sigma_i -\sigma_j\|^2$ given the boundary condition $\sigma_{|\partial \Lambda}$. One key difference between our setting and the continuum is that our main H\"older regularity statement in a large domain $\Lambda\subset \mathbb{Z}^{d=2}$ does not require any regularity assumption on the map $\sigma$ restricted to the boundary of the domain. For example, when $d=2$ and $N=3$, the H\"older regularity induced in the bulk of the domain holds uniformly in all boundary configurations $\sigma \in (\mathbb{S}^{2})^{\partial \Lambda}$ (this is in contrast with the continuum which requires extensions in suitable Sobolev spaces). The fact we obtain results uniformly in the boundary conditions allows us to extend our results for positive temperatures. Namely, as $T \searrow 0$, we obtain a local regularity theory for all infinite volume Spin $O(N)$ Gibbs measures, at least when $d=2$ and $N\geq 3$. We also discuss implications of our analysis in dimensions $d\geq 3$.

papers.title: Generic boundary behavior of Dirichlet eigenfunctions
papers.abstract: We extend Uhlenbeck's classical results on the generic properties of Laplacian eigenfunctions. In particular, we find a residual set of $C^k$ domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $k > n$, such that the nodal set of any Dirichlet eigenfunction intersects the boundary orthogonally along a $C^{k-1}$ embedded submanifold, whenever the intersection is non-empty. This is achieved by analyzing the boundary asymptotics of Dirichlet eigenfunctions via homogeneous harmonic polynomials and comparing their respective nodal sets. Along the way, we give a complete proof that generic Euclidean domains have simple Dirichlet eigenfunctions with zero as a regular value in the interior and zero as a regular value of the boundary normal derivative. In the special case of planar domains, a different argument provides one-parameter families of perturbed domains with the desired properties.

papers.title: Generalized minimizers for the capillarity energy outside convex obstacles
papers.abstract: In general, the capillarity energy outside an unbounded obstacle may fail to admit volume-constrained minimizers, as infimizing sequences may escape to infinity. We study this minimization problem outside a closed convex obstacle $C$. Via a $\Gamma$-convergence result for the capillarity energies outside sequences of closed convex obstacles converging in the Hausdorff sense, we prove that the infimum of the functional is attained by a generalized minimizer, namely, a finite union of regions, each of which minimizes the capillarity energy outside a limit of translations of $C$ in its volume class, with the total volume satisfying the prescribed constraint. Each generalized minimizer can be suitably approximated by an infimizing sequence, thus providing a description of its asymptotic behaviour. As an application, we study the isoperimetric profile associated with the capillarity energy and investigate how the asymptotic geometry of the obstacle affects both this profile and generalized minimizers and their connectedness.

papers.title: Volume growth and parabolicity for non-symmetric operators
papers.abstract: The interplay between a weighted volume measure and its naturally associated weighted Laplace operator is fundamental to the geometric analysis of weighted structures governed by gradient vector fields. Beyond the gradient setting, however, the theory has remained considerably less developed, largely because this natural correspondence is lost. In this paper, we identify invariant measures as the appropriate framework for extending the theory to general drifted Laplace operators. This approach yields a systematic treatment of parabolicity in the non-gradient setting, reveals its connection with volume growth, and leads to new volume finiteness results for non-gradient geometric structures.

papers.title: Global $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimate for complex Monge--Amp\`ere equations on compact K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove a global $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimate for the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation with a positive $C^\alpha$ right-hand side on a compact K\"ahler manifold.

papers.title: Remarks on the disjoint minimal graphs conjecture
papers.abstract: It is known that there can be at most 3 disjoint nontrivial minimal graphs in R^3 with 0 boundary values, and conjectured that there can be at most 2. We explore properties that the graphs would have if there were 3.

papers.title: Auxiliary Hessian Equations
papers.abstract: We propose k-Hessian equations as auxiliary equations for degenera- tions of K\"ahler classes to nef classes of numerical dimension k. As proof-of-concept results, we provide a uniform mean-value inequality and uniform \`a priori estimates for Hessian equa- tions.

papers.title: Stability of Diophantine Minimal Foliations in Arbitrary Codimension
papers.abstract: We generalize Moser's stability theorem for minimal hypersurface foliations to arbitrary codimension. Let $\mathbb{T}^N=\mathbb{R}^N/\mathbb{Z}^N$ be the standard torus, and let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be an $m$-plane satisfying a Diophantine condition relative to $\mathbb{Z}^N$. We prove that, under every sufficiently small smooth $\mathbb{Z}^N$-periodic perturbation of the Euclidean metric, the affine foliation of $\mathbb{T}^N$ induced by $P$ persists as a smoothly conjugate foliation by minimal $m$-dimensional submanifolds. The normalized conjugating displacement depends smoothly and tamely on the metric and is locally unique. The proof uses Hamilton's formulation of the Nash-Moser implicit function theorem.

papers.title: On the Weyl tube formula for nonlocal perimeters
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the nonlocal perimeter of tubular neighbourhoods. For a closed $C^{1,1}$ submanifold of Euclidean space, we show that a suitable rescaling of the nonlocal perimeter of its tube converges to an explicit constant times the Hausdorff measure of the submanifold. The constant is the fractional perimeter of the unit ball in the codimension of the submanifold. For finite point sets, we obtain an exact tube formula in terms of a generalised hypergeometric function. In contrast with the classical Weyl formula, this expansion has infinitely many terms, contains both noninteger and integer powers of the tubular radius, and has coefficients that depend on the relative positions of the points rather than only on their intrinsic geometry. We also establish a point-set expansion for general analytic kernels.

papers.title: On the singular set of the geodesic flow on nonpositively curved surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that the singular locus of the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle of a nonpositively curved surface enjoys an additional regularity property: its characteristic function belongs to the geometric anisotropic Sobolev space $H^{5/8-}_xH^{-13/16}_\theta$. In particular, this implies that if the geodesic flow is not ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure, then the zero set of the curvature must be thick in the sense that it supports a nonzero, nonnegative function in $H^{5/8-}$. The proof relies on semiclassical analysis and a new radial estimate for parabolic flows.

papers.title: Non-algebraicity of the Lawson surfaces $\xi_{k,l}$
papers.abstract: We prove that every Lawson surface $\xi_{k,l}\subset\mathbb S^3$ of genus $kl>1$ is non-algebraic: any real polynomial vanishing on $\xi_{k,l}$ vanishes identically on $\mathbb S^3$. This answers a question posed by Hsiang in 1967 and proves Lawson's 1970 conjecture for $\xi_{2,2}$. The proof uses a reflection principle for the monodromy of the associated family of flat connections.

papers.title: T^2-invariant Einstein metrics on closed 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct $T^2$-invariant Einstein metrics with positive Ricci curvature on #_m(S^2 x S^2) for every integer $m>1$. These provide infinite family of Einstein metrics on closed $4$-manifolds with $\lambda>0$, which are in addition not Hermitian. We further establish the uniqueness of the $T^2$-invariant Einstein metrics on $S^4$, CP^2, S^2 x S^2, and CP^2#\bar{CP}^2.

papers.title: The anisotropic Weyl law and Grassmannian equidistribution
papers.abstract: We establish a Weyl law for the codimension-one anisotropic volume spectrum on compact Riemannian manifolds. We then use this law to obtain equidistribution in the full Grassmannian bundle while keeping the ambient metric fixed. More precisely, on every closed connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension three through six, we construct smooth, embedded hypersurfaces stationary for anisotropies smoothly converging to area. The cumulative sum of their area measures, when lifted to the Grassmannian bundle, converges to the uniform measure.

papers.title: A three-block higher-rank deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills correspondence on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$
papers.abstract: We study the invariant rank-four deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills equation associated with the chain $\mathcal{O}(1)\to\mathcal{O}(2)^{\oplus2}\to\mathcal{O}(3)$ over $\mathbb P^1$, with vertical weights $(4,2,0)$ and a fixed product K\"ahler class and phase. For arbitrary linear arrows $\psi=Bz$ and $\phi=(Az)^T$, smooth strictly calibrated reduced solutions exist exactly when $A$ is invertible and $z^TA^TBz$ is not identically zero. The same condition characterizes stability, semistability and polystability in the specified equivariant coherent category. The classification includes all eleven nonempty coefficient strata and both coincident and distinct divisor points on the rank-one lower boundary. The analytic proof retains the ordered, noncommuting middle equation. After constructing positive-parameter solutions, it rules out unbounded metric values by combining the source budgets with moving spectral tests; on the rank-one lower boundary, the divisor mass must also be retained. Global value, gradient and symbol estimates then give a smooth strictly calibrated endpoint on the original chain. No equivalence with full coherent or derived-category stability, uniqueness, or estimate uniform across changing chains is asserted.

papers.title: Exterior free-boundary minimal surfaces of every topological type with at least two ends
papers.abstract: An exterior free-boundary minimal surface is a properly immersed minimal surface in the complement of the open unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose boundary lies on the unit sphere and meets it orthogonally. We prove that for all integers $\ell\geq2$, $b\geq1$ and $\gamma\geq0$ there is a connected, orientable, properly embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface with $\ell$ ends, $b$ boundary components and genus $\gamma$. Its total curvature is finite, and its ends are parallel catenoidal ends of multiplicity one. By the theorem of Mazet and Mendes, a surface of this kind with one end is a rotational annulus. Hence the topological types of such embedded surfaces are exactly the annulus with one end and all types with at least two ends. There are two gluing constructions. For $\ell\geq3$ we stack $\ell$ sheets over a stable catenoidal annulus that meets the sphere along a circle of radius $4/5$, and we join adjacent sheets by half-catenoidal bridges sitting on the sphere. The sheets are small normal graphs over this annulus whose displacements contain different multiples of the Jacobi field of the family of such annuli, so their boundary circles and the logarithmic growth of their ends differ slightly. For $\ell=2$ we double a catenoidal annulus near the critical angle $\pi/4$, where it acquires a bounded rotationally invariant Jacobi field; the distance to the critical annulus is coupled to the size of the bridges. In gluing constructions inside the unit ball that double or stack a compact surface, the bridges themselves must balance the sheets, which forces many bridges. Here the logarithmic growth of the ends absorbs this balancing. A fixed number of bridges therefore suffices, and every topological type is reached, including the small ones.

papers.title: Injectivity and stability for the sub-Riemannian X-ray transform on H-type groups
papers.abstract: We prove injectivity and a stability estimate for the X-ray transform along sub-Riemannian geodesics of $H$-type groups, a setting in which almost every geodesic carries conjugate points. The geodesics are helices labeled by a charge $\lambda$ valued in the dual of the center. We prove a Fourier slice theorem, which identifies the X-ray transform over geodesics with charge $\lambda$ as the restriction of the group Fourier transform to their visible frequencies, followed by an explicit multiplier. We characterize the sets of charges whose geodesics determine an integrable function, as exactly those whose visible frequencies are dense. In particular, when the center of the group has dimension at least two, charges of a single magnitude suffice provided their directions fill a great circle. Laguerre asymptotics on the spectrum of the normal operator at fixed charge yields a stability estimate at every nonzero visible frequency with the loss of exactly half a derivative in the sub-Laplacian, except on the first Heisenberg group. Finally, we prove that data limited to a band or a cap of charges determines all sufficiently high central frequencies of an unknown function.

papers.title: Nonexistence of minimizers for the second conformal eigenvalue near the round sphere in low dimensions
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of minimizing the second conformal eigenvalue of the conformal Laplacian in a conformal class of metrics with renormalized volume. We prove, in dimensions $n\in\left\{3,\dotsc,10\right\}$, that a minimizer for this problem does not exist for metrics sufficiently close to the round metric on the sphere. This is in striking contrast with the situation in dimensions $n \ge 11$, where Ammann and Humbert obtained the existence of minimizers for the second conformal eigenvalue on any smooth closed non-locally conformally flat manifold. As a byproduct of our techniques, we also obtain a lower bound on the energy of sign-changing solutions of the \nobreak Yamabe equation in dimensions 3, 4 and 5, which extends a result obtained by Weth in the case of the round sphere.

papers.title: Stability of Minkowski-type inequalities in certain warped product spaces
papers.abstract: This paper explores the stability of Minkowski-type inequalities for hypersurfaces in warped product spaces. We establish a stability estimate that bounds the norm of the traceless second fundamental form of the hypersurface in terms of the deficit in the Minkowski inequalities satisfied by the hypersurface. Additionally, we prove the stability of Minkowski inequalities in specific cases of the Reissner-Nordstr\"om Anti-de Sitter (RN-AdS) and Anti-de Sitter Schwarzschild (AdS-Schwarzschild) manifolds, which serve as examples of warped products. We also establish a new rigidity result for locally conformally flat manifolds to understand the stability of these inequalities.

papers.title: A Bernstein Theorem for the Self-Shrinking $J$-Equation and Some Generalizations
papers.abstract: We prove that every entire smooth strictly plurisubharmonic solution of the self-shrinking $J$-equation on $\mathbb{C}^n$ is a quadratic polynomial. This removes the asymptotic lower bound assumption on the complex Hessian in \cite[Theorem 4]{HJ}. The result also recovers the corresponding real rigidity theorem in \cite[Theorem 1.1]{HOW} as a special case. More generally, our method applies to self-shrinking equations associated with a broad class of fully nonlinear elliptic operators satisfying suitable structural conditions, including the adjacent inverse complex Hessian quotient operators $-\sigma_{k-1}/\sigma_{k}$, $1\leq k\leq n$. For the remaining quotients $-\sigma_l/\sigma_k$ with $l<k-1$, we prove the same rigidity conclusion under the additional assumption that the solution is proper.

papers.title: Rigidity and volume pinching for the sharp gradient estimate in positive Ricci curvature
papers.abstract: Colding established a sharp gradient estimate for the Green function on manifolds with non-negative Ricci curvature, which was extended to positive Ricci curvature by Manea recently. We prove almost rigidity of such gradient estimates for positive Ricci curvature. We show that the average of the gradient deficit, namely $\fint (1-|\nabla b|^2)\,dV$, controls the volume deficit in an optimal quantitative manner; here $b$ is the distance-like function defined using the Green function. This implies a quantitative almost rigidity theorem for manifolds with $\ric\ge(n-1)g$ and a gap theorem for Einstein manifolds. We also prove a rigidity theorem for closed 4-dimensional Einstein manifolds by finding a new monotonicity formula.

papers.title: Sharp degree bound for rational proper maps from $\mathbb B^2$ to $\mathbb B^4$
papers.abstract: We prove that every rational proper holomorphic map from $\mathbb{B}^2$ to $\mathbb{B}^4$ has degree at most $5$, confirming D'Angelo's conjecture in this case. This sharp bound follows from Meylan's degree estimates and an intersection-theoretic argument ruling out degree $6$.
